clips.send: A friend who's divorced but still feels weirdly tangled up with their ex, especially over money - relief at learning why, and that it's fixable.
clips.caption:
A legal signature doesn't end a connection. Only the obligation does.

Divorce papers get signed, and that's supposed to be it - except it isn't, not energetically. Two people who never speak again, who've moved on completely, can still be tied to each other for one reason: child support, alimony, any ongoing financial obligation between them. The moment that payment actually stops, Kevin says, the connection breaks clean.

The paperwork was never what held you. The open account was.

Comment RISE and I'll send you how to close one on purpose.
